official_tasks.task: Configure subagent spawning and context passing, remembering that subagents start with isolated context and need findings passed explicitly, with parallel spawns in a single response.
Create team slash commands and skills with the right scope and frontmatter (forked context, tool restrictions, argument hints), and choose skills versus always-loaded CLAUDE.md.
Decide between plan mode and direct execution by task complexity and use the Explore subagent to keep verbose discovery out of the main context.
Run Claude Code in CI non-interactively with structured JSON output, project context via CLAUDE.md, independent review sessions, and de-duplication against prior findings.
Select between synchronous and batch processing by latency tolerance, handle batch failures by correlation id, and size submission windows against an SLA.
Preserve critical facts in long interactions by keeping a persistent case-facts block, trimming verbose tool output, and ordering inputs to counter lost-in-the-middle effects.

Define escalation and ambiguity rules: escalate on explicit human request, policy gaps or stalled progress, ask for more identifiers on multiple matches, and distrust sentiment or self-confidence proxies.
Propagate errors across agents with structured context (failure type, attempt, partial results, alternatives), avoiding both silent suppression and whole-workflow aborts.
Manage context in large-codebase exploration with scratchpad files, subagent delegation, phase summaries, manifest-based crash recovery, and compaction.
Design human review workflows using stratified sampling, per-document-type and per-field accuracy analysis, and calibrated field-level confidence thresholds.
Preserve provenance in multi-source synthesis with claim-source mappings, dated outputs, annotated conflicts, and content-appropriate rendering.
Select a Claude model by weighing capability, latency and cost tradeoffs.
Design system prompts, templates and guardrails.
Apply zero-shot, few-shot and chain-of-thought prompting appropriately.
Optimize context windows and token usage.
Reuse prompts via caching, modular prompts and Skills.
Compare progressive discovery against a monolithic context strategy.
Handle context limits and memory by knowing when to restart, summarize or persist.
Apply common agent patterns (tool-use loops, subagents, memory, context management) and agentic frameworks such as Strands, LangGraph and PydanticAI.

Operate Claude Code core pieces (rules, skills, commands, agents, agent memory) and features such as sessions, slash commands, headless and streaming modes and auto mode, plus repo initialization and settings.json.
Explain LLM fundamentals (tokens, context window, sampling, non-determinism), model modes (fast mode, extended and adaptive thinking, effort levels) and zero/single/multi-shot prompting.
Control context with window management, drift and bloat prevention (tool-output pruning, compaction) and isolation via subagents or multi-step workflows.
Engineer prompts with clear instructions, few-shot examples, system-vs-user placement, output constraints, iterative refinement and input sanitization.
Produce, validate and consume Claude output using structured output, response validation, defensive parsing and skepticism toward confident answers.

docs_facts.fact: Server-side clearing of old context, beta header context-management-2025-06-27. Two strategies: clear_tool_uses_20250919 (clear oldest tool results) and clear_thinking_20251015 (manage earlier thinking blocks). The docs call server-side compaction the primary strategy for long conversations and context editing the fine-grained option. Clearing invalidates cached prefixes, so use clear_at_least to make it worthwhile.

Strategy type for tool-result clearing, used as {type: clear_tool_uses_20250919} inside context_management.edits. Defaults: trigger 100,000 input tokens (or tool_uses), keep 3 most recent tool use/result pairs, exclude_tools none, clear_tool_inputs false (only results are cleared, calls stay). Cleared results are replaced by placeholder text.
Top-level request parameter holding an edits array of strategies, sent with beta header context-management-2025-06-27 (client.beta.messages in SDKs).

Server-side summarisation that replaces older turns with a summary. Two API forms: compaction on demand (you request a summary and put the returned block first in messages; beta header compact-2026-09-04 and a top-level compaction parameter) and compaction at a token threshold (API triggers it inside ordinary requests when input tokens reach your trigger; no background run). Client-side compaction in the tool runner was removed in API version 2026-10-21 (migration guide). Claude Code's own /compact and auto-compaction: not verified here.
docs_facts.exam_era_risk: Compaction is a September 2026 API addition (header compact-2026-09-04) and the tool-runner client-side compaction was removed 2026-10-21; older material describes only context editing or client-side summarising.

docs_facts.fact: Client-side tool: add {type: memory_20250818, name: memory}; Claude issues file commands against a /memories directory and your code executes them and returns tool_result. Commands: view, create, str_replace, insert, delete, rename. Your handler must reject paths outside /memories (path traversal), and you own storage, size and expiry. Pairs with context editing/compaction for long-running agents.
